doc.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Max Roach in the big band
summary: Roach's innovative drumming made it hard to find the one, and the band had to sneak back in after his solos.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: While we’re dealing with some of these so-called young turks, I guess they call them, that popped up in your band in the forties, you mentioned Max Roach. You couldn’t recall exactly how he joined, but . . .
How about his drumming style and how it fit in with the orchestra? What was that like?

Eventually it fit in, but it was very strange to me, because it was one of those, at the time he was so innovative that it was hard to know where one was, as I said before, you know. Let me know where one is, and I’ll find two on my own. But he had a tremendous technique then, you know, that has really developed into something by now.
Would you feature him at that time on drum solos much?
And that’s where you had trouble finding out where he was . . .
We had to sneak back in, you know, after one of his solos.
What about driving a big band? This was probably the first time he had been in that musical setting.
